correctness.rationale: For a centered f-prime(1)=1/2 Kubo–Ando mean, its harmonic representing measure ν has m1=0, and exactly r+ = log H(tanh(r/2))−log H(−tanh(r/2)) for H(u)=∫(1−tu)^−1dν. Uniqueness of moments on compact [-1,1] says all odd moments vanish iff ν is reflection-symmetric, yielding one-step equality. Otherwise the first odd nonzero m_p, p>=3, gives r+ = m_p r^p/2^(p−1)+O(r^(p+2)), ruling out even finite orders. Strict internality of both outputs ensures global convergence of positive two-periodic weights, with conditioned superexponential profile from logarithmic iteration. Legendre densities (1+εP_p)/2 for odd p>=3, ε in (0,1), have exactly vanishing preceding odd moments, coefficient 2ε(p!)²/(2p+1)!, and strictly positive odd-tail moments prevent finite diagonal hits. Independently checked rational Legendre moments p=3,5,7 at ε=3/5, obtaining r coefficients 3/350,1/2310,1/42900. No extrapolation of finite moments to all orders.

originality.rationale: The induced Aluthge transform and convergence for centered operators appear in Osaka–Yamazaki arXiv:2409.03338, especially Theorem 2.7 and Theorem 3.3. The published Resultary Nov2 cyclic nonlinear spectral-rate theorem identifies the vanishing linear factor and supergeometric convergence at λ=1/2,m=2, but not first nonzero odd moment, every possible superattraction order, sharp coefficient and constructive Legendre realizations. The exact countable hierarchy is an additional local dynamical classification; searched for equivalent moment-flat means.
residual_risks: The nonlinear odd-moment hierarchy is restricted to strictly positive two-periodic weights; it is not a theorem for all centered operators.
An unindexed deeper comparison within nonlinear mean iteration may contain an equivalent higher-order classification; the Osaka–Yamazaki paper was read in relevant sections rather than exhaustively.
